title: A systems herbal-to-molecule and transcriptomic strategy identifies emodin as an ESR1-targeting phytochemical driving thrombopoiesis.
authors: Qi, Xiao; Li, Qinyao; Li, Fengyu; Zhou, Linglin; Mo, Qi; Zeng, Jing; Hu, Tianci; Liu, Sheng; Mei, Xinyue; Wu, Min; Qiang, Xuejing; Cheng, Qiyang; Wu, Anguo; Zhou, Xiaogang; Huang, Feihong; Wang, Qiaozhi; Chen, Peng; Wu, Jianming; Wang, Long
one_liner_zh: 该文通过组学与分子对接/MD模拟发现大黄素靶向ESR1促进血小板生成，虽涉及蛋白-配体对接与MD，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，仅间接涉及转录因子下游，与本课题TF-DNA结合建模关联较弱。
abstract: Radiation-induced thrombocytopenia (RIT) is a major dose-limiting toxicity of radiotherapy, for which effective pharmacological interventions remain limited. Rhei Radix et Rhizoma (RR) is widely used in traditional medicine, yet its thrombopoietic activity and molecular basis have not been systematically defined. Here, we investigated the effects of RR on thrombopoiesis using an integrated herbal-to-molecule and transcriptomic strategy. RR extract and representative phytochemicals were screened for megakaryocyte (MK) differentiation in Meg-01, K562, and murine haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), followed by validation in a mouse RIT model. Network pharmacology and transcriptomic analyses indicated that RR regulates thrombopoiesis through coordinated multi-pathway modulation. Emodin was identified as the principal bioactive constituent mediating these effects. Functionally, emodin promoted MK maturation and polyploidization in vitro, accelerated megakaryopoiesis and platelet recovery in irradiated mice. Integrated target prediction and experimental validation identified ESR1 as a direct functional target of emodin, supported by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, CETSA, and DARTS assays. Mechanistically, emodin activated ESR1-dependent PI3K/AKT and JAK2/STAT3 signaling, leading to induction of lineage-specific transcription factors and enhanced platelet biogenesis. Collectively, these findings identify emodin as a key thrombopoietic constituent of RR and reveal an ESR1-centered regulatory axis in megakaryopoiesis, supporting its therapeutic potential for RIT.
abstract_zh: 放射性诱导的血小板减少症（RIT）是放射治疗的主要剂量限制性毒性，目前有效的药物干预手段仍然有限。大黄（Rhei Radix et Rhizoma, RR）在传统医学中广泛应用，但其促血小板生成活性及分子基础尚未被系统阐明。本研究采用整合的草药-分子及转录组学策略，探讨了RR对血小板生成的影响。在Meg-01、K562和小鼠造血干祖细胞（HSPCs）中筛选了RR提取物及代表性植物化学物质对巨核细胞（MK）分化的作用，并在小鼠RIT模型中进行了验证。网络药理学和转录组学分析表明，RR通过协调的多通路调节调控血小板生成。大黄素（emodin）被鉴定为介导这些效应的主要生物活性成分。功能上，大黄素在体外促进MK成熟和多倍体化，在受照射小鼠中加速巨核细胞生成和血小板恢复。综合靶点预测和实验验证确定ESR1为大黄素的直接功能靶点，并通过分子对接、分子动力学模拟、CETSA和DARTS实验得到支持。机制上，大黄素激活ESR1依赖的PI3K/AKT和JAK2/STAT3信号通路，导致谱系特异性转录因子的诱导和血小板生物合成的增强。总体而言，这些发现将大黄素鉴定为RR的关键促血小板生成成分，并揭示了巨核细胞生成中以ESR1为中心的调控轴，支持其在RIT中的治疗潜力。
